desk.headline: Revenue down 1.8% to KRW 7.0tn, slightly above estimates; operating profit down 6.1%; dividend floor kept
results: Revenue slipped 1.8% to KRW 7.0tn, against a year-ago quarter boosted by a property project and hurt this time by a customer reward programme that cut wireless income.
Operating income fell 6.1% to KRW 505.3bn and net income 17.5% to KRW 367.3bn; KT says profit rose excluding last year's one-off property gain.
Wireless service revenue fell 3.9%, but total mobile subscribers rose 6.1% to 30.1m and KT-network (MNO) users grew 1.4% from Q2 to 20.7m.
AI and digital (AX) revenue grew 11.9% to KRW 1.11tn over nine months; kt cloud revenue rose 7.7% and kt estate 39.1%.
A Q3 dividend of KRW 600 per share was declared and a KRW 250bn share buyback was completed in September.

guidance.summary: KT gave no revenue or profit forecast for Q4 or 2026. It kept its promise of at least KRW 2,400 in dividends per share for 2026 and its target to more than double AX revenue by 2028 from 2025.

points: Management described a gradual recovery in mobile subscribers and ARPU now the reward programme is over, but warned beating last year's consumer results will be hard.
Business orders were up more than 20% year to date, helped by data-centre demand and wins in banking, defence and healthcare.
KT plans to grow AI data-centre capacity from about 152 MW to 1 GW by 2031, mostly leased rather than owned.
AI is already cutting customer-service staffing needs; management will put numbers on the cost savings next year.
KT restated plans for KRW 1tn of buybacks by 2028 and a 9–10% return on equity, helped by selling non-core assets.
call.source: Results presentation (Exhibit 99.1) and call coverage: Motley Fool transcript, 10 Nov 2026; Herald Business, 10 Nov 2026

watch: Whether mobile ARPU and wireless revenue turn up in Q4 after the reward programme.
Progress and funding of the AI data-centre build-out.
The year-end dividend and further buybacks or asset sales.
